description: TaskTick is a free, open-source native macOS app for scheduling scripts, managing background services, and inspecting execution logs. Make room for what matters.

features.title: Less to manage.
features.subtitle: More room to create.
features.description:
From a one-off script to an always-on service,
keep it all in one familiar Mac interface.

items.title: Scheduling that makes sense
items.description: Pick a date, time, or repeat cycle, or use a Cron expression. Import your existing crontab tasks in a click.

items.title: Your scripts, ready to go
items.description: Write a script inline or choose a local .sh, .py, .rb, or .js file. Put your familiar tools to work automatically.

items.title: A home for background services
items.description: Start and stop long-running commands. Configure app-start behavior, restart policies, file logs, and size-based rotation.

items.title: Every run, accounted for
items.description: Inspect standard output, errors, exit codes, and execution time. Know what happened without digging through terminals.

items.title: The results come to you
items.description: Choose success or failure notifications for each task. Get results through native macOS notifications.

items.title: Feels like your Mac
items.description: Built with SwiftUI and always close in your menu bar. English and Chinese interfaces, on Apple Silicon and Intel.

items.question: Is TaskTick free?
items.answer: Yes. TaskTick is free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license. Explore the source, report an issue, or contribute on GitHub.

items.question: Will it work on my Mac?
items.answer: TaskTick requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Downloads are available for both Apple Silicon and Intel. Choose the matching DMG on the release page.

items.question: Do tasks run after I close the window?
items.answer: Yes. TaskTick can stay in your menu bar and schedule tasks after the main window closes. Keep the app running; scripts cannot execute while your Mac is shut down or asleep. Check execution logs for results.

items.question: What about my existing crontab?
items.answer: Use the in-app Crontab Import feature to bring system crontab tasks into TaskTick. Review the original entries to avoid running the same task in both places.

items.question: What if macOS shows a security prompt?
items.answer: Check the signing and notarization notes on the corresponding GitHub Release. An unnotarized build may require right-clicking TaskTick.app in Finder and choosing Open. See the project's installation instructions for details.
